text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Shares ended higher for a third day, as worries over next week's budget eased and nerves were calmed by a firm early showing on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,657.9, up 17.9 points, or 0.39 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares notched up more records as the blue chip DAX reached an all-time high close, but profit-taking took the edge off the market's advance. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,805.29, up 6.78 points, or 0.18 percent.

PARIS - Stocks hit a record closing high, with Rhone-Poulenc shares leaping nearly 20 percent after news that the chemicals and drugs firm planned to buy out its U.S. subsidiary Rhone-Poulenc Rorer. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,893.64, up 26.20 points, or 0.91 percent.
ZURICH - Shares managed another record close though they slipped back from earlier gains. The Swiss market index closed at 5,669.9, up 7.5 points, or 0.13 percent.
TOKYO - Stocks edged lower as an upbeat mood carried over from the previous day finally fizzled out. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,624.76, down 54.51 points, or 0.26 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks rose but gains were trimmed by investors taking profits before the three-day market holiday next week marking Hong Kong's handover on July 1, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,128.02, up 63 points, or 0.42 percent.
SYDNEY - Shares closed slightly weaker, with the All Ordinaries index at 2,699.9, down 5.2 points, or 0.19 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - The industrial and all-share indices finished at record highs, boosted by a host of positive news. The all-share index closed at 7,402.7, up 48.7 points, or 0.66 percent, the all Gold index closed at 1,008.8, up 1.4 points, while the industrial index closed at 8,742.3, up 72.4 points, or 0.84 percent.
